crucialFeats: One-inch punch demonstration at Long Beach
1958 inter-school boxing title win over Gary Elms
Built Jeet Kune Do by effectively combining multiple styles

dossier.advantage: Extremely trained body and inhuman speed. He possesses total muscle control, allowing him to deliver powerful strikes from zero distance.
dossier.mentality: Instant adaptation and instinctive precision. He reads the opponent's intentions in a fraction of a second, striking where the defense is weakest, without adhering to rigid patterns.
dossier.style: Masterful synthesis of Jeet Kune Do. Bruce Lee combines boxing, fencing, and Wing Chun into one fluid system, eliminating unnecessary movements in favor of direct interception of the enemy's attack.

fighterA.name: Character A

powers: Elite human speed, reflexes, coordination, and precision striking.
tools: JKD interception timing, low kicks, rhythm disruption, and cross-style adaptation.
weaknesses: Significant size and reach deficit versus heavyweight specialists.

crucialFeats: Defeated 21 champions or heavyweight title challengers.

dossier.advantage: Heavyweight durability and ring intelligence. He can take a punch, but his true strength lies in avoiding them and dictating the fight's pace.
dossier.mentality: A charismatic showman with a will of steel. He provokes the opponent to throw them off balance and methodically break their confidence.
dossier.quote: Float like a butterfly, sting like a bee.
dossier.style: Masterful control of distance and rhythm. He uses legendary footwork and a quick command of the ring to frustrate enemies and score points from a safe distance.

fighterB.name: Character B

powers: Elite heavyweight boxing speed, timing, durability, and ring IQ.
tools: Jab control, footwork, defensive movement, clinch management, and pacing control.
weaknesses: Primarily boxing-centric toolkit compared with broad open-rule combat sets.

fight-simulation.opening: Bruce attacks rhythm with fast entries and low-line disruption before Ali can settle the ring geography.
fight-simulation.mid_fight: Ali taxes distance with the jab, feet, and ring control, forcing Bruce to pay for every re-entry.
fight-simulation.late_fight: The fight either stays ugly and narrow for Bruce or settles into repeatable heavyweight distance, where Ali's durability and pace take over.
fight-simulation.end_condition: If Bruce cannot keep the fight tight and ugly, true heavyweight distance starts working for Ali with every minute.
fight-simulation.phase_1_event: Bruce attacks rhythm with fast entries and low-line disruption before Ali can settle the ring geography.
fight-simulation.phase_2_event: Ali taxes distance with the jab, feet, and ring control, forcing Bruce to pay for every re-entry.
fight-simulation.phase_2_branch_a: Bruce keeps the entries short and irregular, so Ali never gets to set the full ring geography.
fight-simulation.phase_2_branch_b: Ali establishes the jab, feet, and rhythm, so every Bruce re-entry starts costing more.
fight-simulation.phase_3_event: The fight either stays ugly and narrow for Bruce or settles into repeatable heavyweight distance, where Ali's durability and pace take over.
fight-simulation.phase_3_branch_a: Bruce keeps the fight dirty, tight, and outside full heavyweight distance.
fight-simulation.phase_3_branch_b: The fight settles into repeatable heavyweight distance, where Ali's pace and durability take over.

final-summary.line_1: Ali owns the paper comparison, 87.67 vs 78.89.
final-summary.line_2: Bruce changes the texture of the fight more than the winner identity.
final-summary.line_3: Open rules narrow the matchup, but do not flip the baseline result.

stat-trap.question: Can Bruce stop the fight from turning into Ali's range-and-tax pattern?
stat-trap.trap_bottom: DO NOT REPLACE REACH AND DURABILITY
stat-trap.example: Bruce's best edges change the texture of the fight more than the winner identity. Speed and style can win moments, but Ali's proof under sustained heavyweight pressure is the real separator.

tactical-board.lane: Bruce wins by keeping the fight unstable. Ali wins by making every exchange look like heavyweight reality.
tactical-board.subtitle: Artist versus Boxer

interpretation.line_1: Bruce owns speed, disruption, and the uglier opening texture.
interpretation.line_2: Ali owns the categories that settle repeated human exchanges: reach, durability, pacing, and ring management.
interpretation.line_3: Bruce only narrows the matchup if he prevents the fight from hardening into Ali's preferred distance game.

battle-dynamics.phase_1: Bruce is live early because speed and disruption matter most before the fight settles.
battle-dynamics.phase_2: Ali steadies the exchanges once reach and pacing begin to dictate range.
battle-dynamics.phase_3: Ali grows stronger as range, pacing, and durability compound over repeated exchanges.
battle-dynamics.analysis: Bruce is live early because speed and disruption matter most before the fight settles. Ali grows stronger as range, pacing, and durability compound over repeated exchanges.
